summary: Lars Fogelin specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli and held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1971–1984) as well as the Universities of Heidelberg and Bonn, later teaching at the University of Oslo (~1998–2003).

Lata S. Bapat is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She completed her PhD under M. P. Marathe at Savitribai Phule Pune University by 1985, where she was attested as a Research Associate in Buddhist Philosophy in 1989.

Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ganden, Ganden Shartse, and Gyuto monasteries, served as abbot of Ganden and Ganden Shartse (~1976–1985), and was a Visiting Scholar at the University of Virginia (~1976–1977).
Latika Lahiri is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Xianlin Ji (~1956–1960) and at Peking University (1958) before holding a post at the University of Delhi (~1969–1988).

Laura Harrington works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman, alongside teachers including Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi, Gary A. Tubb, and Lobsang Jamspal.

Lauran Hartley is a Tibetologist who has served as an adjunct lecturer at Columbia University and a visiting assistant professor at Indiana University. She also held posts at Rutgers University and the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (both attested 2003).

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. After medical studies at the University of Glasgow (~1874–1878), he served in the Indian Medical Service and Indian Army (~1880–1917) and was Professor of Tibetan at UCL (1906–1908).

Laurence Binyon (1869–1943) worked in Japanology and Sinology. Educated at St Paul's School and Trinity College, Oxford (~1888–1892), he held long-term posts at the British Museum (~1893–1933) and Harvard University (~1933–1934).

Laurence Khantipalo Mills (1932–2021) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Jianmin Chen, Dhardo Rinpoche, Acharya Buddharakkhita, Dudjom Rinpoche, Sangharakshita, and Namkhai Norbu. He served as abbot at Wat Buddha Dhamma beginning in 1978.

Laurie L. Patton is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at Harvard and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1986–1991), she held professorships at Emory and Duke, and served as president of Middlebury College (2015–2024) and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a religious studies scholar. He served as Director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as a professor in the Department of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837–1918) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at New York University and served as a professor at the University of Oxford until 1918.

Lawrence William Nelson works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at numerous institutions, including Butler, Indiana, New York, and Northwestern Universities, earning a doctorate in philosophy and religion from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2012).
Laxmanshastri Joshi (1901–1994) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Kevalananda Saraswati (~1916–1923) and served as Director of Prajna Pathashala from ~1948 to 1994.

LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed studies at Washington and Lee University (~1895–1898) and Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903), where he studied under Maurice Bloomfield.

Leah Judith Zahler was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia, where she studied under Jeffrey Hopkins, Harvey B. Aronson, Joe Bransford Wilson, and Ngawang Wangyal.

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. In 2011, he was attested as Professor Emeritus of Anthropology at Drew University and as a Research Associate in anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

Leela Aditi Wood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who held a post at Deccan College. She completed her PhD at the University of Michigan in 2005 under doctoral supervisors Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers.

Leo Frobenius (1873–1938) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He held posts at the Frobenius Institute (1920–1938), Goethe University Frankfurt (1932–1938), Museum der Weltkulturen (1935–1938), and the Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte.
